newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN MONEY DEMAND RISES, BANKS LOOK TO C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN MONEY DEMAND RISES, BANKS LOOK TO C.BANK.

text.p: The Croatian money market demand rose on Monday ahead of the monthly pension payment and banks were looking to the central bank for help, dealers said.
Banks' accounts thinned down over the weekend, shrinking supply by the usual creditors to 45 million kuna from roughly double that in the past week or so.
Some 35.3 million fresh loans, mostly call money at a steady 7.0 percent, were settled by 0900 GMT.

"The interbank supply is not so strong today, and there are no term funds on offer," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters. "It sufficed to meet the reported demand. But banks are a little nervous of the pensions (payouts)."

The state pension fund began gave orders for the July pension payment today after a few days' delay as it sought to husband its resources, scarcer this month because of late contributions by companies.

With less than 600 million kuna on their balances, against their own clients' orders and a strong outflow of kuna due to exchange operations, the banks expected the central bank to bail them out through an intervention to boost money supply.

It can do it by purchasing hard currency or repurchasing outstanding bills, for which it would inject kuna two days later -- before Friday's bank holiday. But the bank had no intervention planned yet, an official told Reuters. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
